Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.

Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
In what year did Johann Wolfgang von Goethe die?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 – 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
In what year was Nitrogen discovered?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
Which company manufactures Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk?
Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk: Skunk Works. It was the first operational aircraft to be designed with stealth technology.
Which country is Panavia Tornado from?
Panavia Tornado: Italy. It first flew on 14 August 1974 and was introduced into service in 1979–1980.
Who is credited with discovering Pavo?
Pavo (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Pavo is a constellation in the southern sky whose name is Latin for 'peacock'.
Who is credited with discovering Nitroglycerin?
Nitroglycerin: Ascanio Sobrero. It is combined with nitrocellulose to form double-based smokeless powder, used as a propellant in artillery and firearms since the 1880s.
Who is credited with discovering Lithium?
Lithium: Johan August Arfwedson. Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

The only living member of its entire taxonomic order, this nocturnal African mammal digs into termite and ant hills using sharp claws and powerful legs — related distantly to elephants and manatees, what is it?
Aardvark (Orycteropus afer) is a medium-sized, burrowing, nocturnal mammal native to Africa.
A pioneer of industrial toxicology, this American physician trained at Michigan, worked out of Hull House in Chicago, and led the fight to curb lead poisoning in the workplace — who was she?
Alice Hamilton (February 27, 1869 - September 22, 1970) was an American physician, research scientist, and author.
Nicknamed the 'nail mosquito,' this genus — first classified in 1818 — is the sole mosquito genus known to carry human malaria — which genus is it?
Anopheles is a genus of mosquito first described by the German entomologist J. W. Meigen in 1818.
About a third of the several hundred mold species in this genus have a sexual reproductive stage, and some cause infections while others hold commercial value — which genus?
Aspergillus is a genus consisting of several hundred mold species found in various climates worldwide.
Ranging from 1 to 5 meters tall and found across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas, this shrub genus's best-known species is the European type also called barberry — what genus is it?
Berberis is a large genus of deciduous and evergreen shrubs from 1-5 m (3+12-16+12 ft) tall, found throughout temperate and subtropical regions of the world (apart from Australia).
This branch of biology studies how plants have grown, reproduced, and evolved over the last 3.5 billion years of life on Earth — what field is it?
Botany is the branch of natural science and biology that studies the growth, reproduction and evolution of plants over the last 3.5 billion years of life on earth.

The largest land bird in North America went fully extinct in the wild in 1987 when every survivor was captured for breeding — which critically endangered vulture has since returned to the Grand Canyon and beyond?
California condor (Gymnogyps californianus) is a New World vulture and the largest North American land bird.

Appearing in early childhood with symptoms like poor coordination and stiff or weak muscles, this group of movement disorders does not worsen over time even though symptoms become more noticeable in a child's first years — which condition?
Cerebral palsy (CP) is a group of movement disorders that appear in early childhood.
This tangor — a mandarin-orange cross — typically splits into seven to fourteen easy-to-peel segments — which fruit?
Clementine (Citrus clementina) is a tangor, a citrus fruit hybrid between a willowleaf mandarin orange (C. deliciosa) and a sweet orange (C. sinensis).
Born in 1863, this Italian mathematician is remembered chiefly as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry — who was he?
Corrado Segre (20 August 1863 - 18 May 1924) was an Italian mathematician who is remembered today as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry.
Affecting some 280 million people worldwide, this state of low mood saps motivation and the pleasure once taken in activities — what is it?
Depression (mood) is a mental state of low mood and aversion to activity.
Sometimes triggered by lead poisoning or reactions to neuroleptic drugs, this neurological disorder produces involuntary, twisting muscle contractions — what is it?

Dystonia is a neurological hyperkinetic movement disorder in which sustained or repetitive muscle contractions occur involuntarily, resulting in twisting and repetitive movements or abnormal fixed postures.
This Ancient Greek polymath, who became chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria, is considered the founder of geography as a discipline and coined much of its early terminology — who is he?
The excessive buildup of collagen-rich connective tissue after chronic inflammation or repeated injury, leaving a permanent scar that can choke off organ function — what's this process called?
Fibrosis is the development of fibrous connective tissue in response to an injury.
Sometimes mistakenly called the 'stomach flu' even though it's unrelated to influenza, this inflammation of the gut is usually viral, with rotavirus the top cause in children. What condition is it?
Gastroenteritis is an inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract including the stomach and intestine.
The first of America's Teen Series fighters, this twin-tail jet with swing wings debuted at sea on the USS Enterprise in 1974. What is it?
Grumman F-14 Tomcat is an American carrier-capable supersonic, twin-engine, tandem two-seat, twin-tail, all-weather-capable variable-sweep wing fighter aircraft.
Nicknamed the giant crab spider or cane spider, this member of the huntsman spider family is native to the tropics but has spread into subtropical areas — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria is a species of spider in the family Sparassidae, the huntsman spiders.
About the size of an almond in humans, this small brain region links the nervous system to the endocrine system via the pituitary gland — what is it?
Hypothalamus (pl.: hypothalami; from Ancient Greek (hup) 'under' and (thlamos) 'chamber') is a small part of the vertebrate brain that contains a number of nuclei with a variety of functions.
The biggest cat in the Americas, it kills with a bite so powerful it can crack a turtle's shell — or punch straight through a mammal's skull between the ears. Which spotted predator is it?
Jaguar (Panthera onca) is a large cat species and the only living member of the genus Panthera that is native to the Americas.
This Indian aerospace engineer served as secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of both ISRO and the Space Commission — who is he?
K. Sivan (born 14 April 1957) is an Indian aerospace engineer who served as the secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of ISRO and Space Commission.

Seen using a silver stain and grown on media containing the amino acid cysteine, this genus of bacteria causes a severe pneumonia-like illness as well as a milder flu-like illness called Pontiac fever — name the genus?
Legionella is a genus of Gram-negative bacteria that can be seen using a silver stain or grown in a special media that contains cysteine, an amino acid.

Fatigue, memory problems, breathlessness, and sleep trouble that the WHO marks as setting in three months after infection — symptoms that vanish and reappear for weeks or years. What condition is this?
Long COVID is a group of health problems persisting or developing after an initial period of COVID19 from 2 infection.
An autosomal dominant flaw in the fibrillin-making FBN1 gene gives this disorder its tell-tale look — tall, long-limbed, double-jointed — while quietly threatening the aorta — what is it?
Marfan syndrome (MFS) is a multi-systemic genetic disorder that affects the connective tissue.
This British-Lebanese geometer co-founded topological K-theory and lent his name to a famous index theorem — and won both the Fields Medal and the Abel Prize. Who was he?
Michael Atiyah (22 April 1929 - 11 January 2019) was a British-Lebanese mathematician specialising in geometry.

Though its 83 species can grow as tall as trees, this genus is technically herbaceous, its 'trunk' just tightly wrapped leaf stalks, and it gives us edible bananas, plantains, and fiber for cloth — what genus is it?
Musa (plant) is one of three genera in the family Musaceae.
This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats acute pain and osteoarthritis by blocking prostaglandin production, though it carries a risk of liver side effects. Name the drug?
Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with pain medication and fever reducing properties.

Believed to be the world's fourth-leading cause of disability, this condition wears down joint cartilage over years, often first striking the knuckles nearest your fingertips and the base of the thumb — what is it?
Osteoarthritis is a type of degenerative joint disease that results from breakdown of joint cartilage and underlying bone.

Also known as underage medicine, this branch of medicine covers care from infancy through adolescence — typically up to age 18 in most of the Commonwealth, but only 12 in India. Name the medical specialty?

Pediatrics (American English), also spelled paediatrics (British English) and also known as underage medicine, is the branch of medicine that involves the medical care of infants, toddlers, children, adolescents, and young adults.
When this domesticated mammal reached Europe from the Near East, it interbred so freely with local wild boar that scholars still argue whether it's a distinct species — what animal is it?
Pig (Sus domesticus), also called swine (pl.: swine) or hog, is an omnivorous, domesticated, even-toed, hoofed mammal.

Caused by the loss of function of specific genes on chromosome 15, this rare genetic disorder leads to weak muscles and poor feeding in infancy, then constant hunger and risk of obesity in childhood — what's it called?

Prader–Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare genetic disorder caused by a loss of function of specific genes on chromosome 15. A similar mechanism occurs in Angelman syndrome, except the defective chromosome 15 is from the mother, or two copies are from the father.
This white, odorless nitroamine explosive, widely used since World War II, is the explosive agent inside C-4 plastic explosive — what is it called?
RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
Made by steaming dehusked oat groats before flattening them under heavy rollers and lightly toasting them, this whole-grain food becomes porridge when cooked — which product?
Rolled oats are a type of lightly processed whole-grain food.
Caused by a lack of vitamin C, this deficiency disease shows up after about a month of poor diet with weakness, sore limbs, gum disease, and bleeding from the skin — what is it?
Scurvy is a deficiency disease (state of malnutrition) resulting from a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid).
Unlike its shelled cousin the snail, this soft-bodied land mollusk gets by with no shell at all, or at most a tiny internal remnant of one — what animal is it?
Slug is a common name for any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc.
This Taiwanese-American software engineer co-founded and served as CTO of a massively popular video-sharing platform before later building MixBit through his company AVOS Systems — who is he?
Steve Chen (Wade-; born August 25, 1978) is a Taiwanese-American software engineer and Internet entrepreneur who is a co-founder and ex-CTO of YouTube.
Defined as applying conceptual knowledge to reach practical goals in a repeatable way, this field covers both tangible machines and intangible things like software — what is it?
Technology is the application of conceptual knowledge to achieve practical goals, especially in a reproducible way.
What's the name for hardened, foul-smelling deposits of trapped debris that form in the crevices of the tonsils, sometimes visible as white flecks at the back of the throat?
Tonsil stones are mineralizations of debris within the crevices of the tonsils.
Occasionally causing hearing loss or bone marrow suppression as side effects, this IV antibiotic treats MRSA infections and, in oral form, a common gut infection - which drug?
Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic medication used to treat certain bacterial infections.
Short-legged, muscular, and stubby-tailed, this Australian marsupial can reach about a metre long and tip the scales between 20 and 35 kilograms — what is it?
Wombat are short-legged, muscular quadrupedal marsupials of the family Vombatidae that are native to Australia.
Found naturally in coffee, bread and ripe fruit, this aldehyde is produced when your liver partly oxidizes ethanol — making it a chief culprit behind the hangover. What is it?

Born as a Spanish CASA design and now built by a major European aerospace conglomerate, this twin-engine turboprop transport plane first flew in November 1997 and entered Spanish Air Force service in 1999 — which aircraft?
Airbus C295: European tactical military transport aircraft.
Nicknamed the death cap, this deadly poisonous fungus resembles edible species like Caesar's mushroom and is native to Europe — what is it?
Amanita phalloides: Poisonous mushroom (death cap). The large fruiting bodies appear in summer and autumn; the caps are generally greenish in colour with a white stipe and gills.
Native to the eastern Mediterranean, this flowering herb's seeds taste similar to fennel, licorice, and tarragon and flavor candies and spirits — what is it?
Also called gobō, this Eurasian plant is cultivated in Japan for its edible root but has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils elsewhere — which species?
Arctium lappa: Species of flowering plant. It has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils in North America, Australia, and other regions, but is cultivated for its vegetable root.
Developed to herd livestock across rough terrain by nipping at their heels, this short-coated working breed's coat reads as either 'red' or 'blue' — which breed?

Australian Cattle Dog: Breed of herding dog. The Australian Cattle Dog, or simply Cattle Dog, is a breed of herding dog developed in Australia for droving cattle over long distances across rough terrain.
With more than 2,000 species and petals but no sepals, this flowering plant genus originated in Africa and is popular as an ornamental houseplant in cooler climates — which genus?
Begonia: Genus of perennial flowering plants.
This medium-sized antelope of India and Nepal sports corkscrew horns up to 30 inches long and a striking two-tone coat, with white around the eyes set against black face stripes — which animal?
Blackbuck: Antelope native to India and Nepal. The blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), also known as the Indian antelope, is a medium-sized antelope native to India and Nepal.

This infraorder of decapod crustaceans tucks a stubby tail-like abdomen under a hard shell and ends its front pair of legs in pincers — over 1.5 million tonnes of them are eaten by humans yearly. What group is it?
Brachyura: Crustacean. The true crabs are the largest of the crab decapod groups with carcinised body forms.
A cole crop related to broccoli, cauliflower and Brussels sprouts, the heaviest recorded head of this leafy vegetable weighed nearly 138 pounds — what is it?
Cabbage: Leafy vegetable in the flowering plant family Brassicaceae.
This infraorder of decapod crustaceans is the true taxonomic home of what everyone actually calls a shrimp, found in fresh and salt water worldwide — what is it?
The largest part of the brain, this structure houses the cerebral cortex plus the hippocampus and basal ganglia, and works with the cerebellum to control every voluntary action. What is it?
Cerebrum: Large part of the brain containing the cerebral cortex.
Selected from over 11,000 applicants for NASA's Teacher in Space Project, this Concord, New Hampshire educator died aboard the Challenger in 1986 — who was she?
Christa McAuliffe: American teacher and astronaut (1948–1986)
Found naturally in the sap of the opium poppy, this opiate is a prodrug of morphine often paired with paracetamol to treat mild pain, coughs, and even diarrhea — what is it?
Codeine: Opiate and prodrug of morphine used to treat pain. It usually starts working after half an hour, with maximum effect at two hours.
Also known as the Cornelian cherry, this dogwood-family shrub or small tree is native to western and southern Europe as well as southwestern Asia — what's its scientific name?
Cornus mas: Species of flowering plant in the family Cornaceae.
This closed sac in the body, distinct from an abscess of pus, forms a shell of abnormal cells and may contain air, fluid, or semi-solid material — what is it, medically?
Cyst: Closed sac growth on the body. A cyst is a closed sac in the body, having a distinct envelope and division compared with the nearby tissue.
Native to South and Southeast Asia, this is the sole species in its genus and lives in large, non-hierarchical clans with several breeding females — what's this wild canid called?
Dhole: Species of mammal. The dhole ( dohl; Cuon alpinus) is a canid native to South, East and Southeast Asia.

Aristotle's Poetics contrasted this performance-based mode with the epic and the lyrical, and its name comes from a Greek word meaning "deed" or "act" — the two-masks symbol marks its split into comedy and tragedy. What is it?
Drama: Artwork intended for performance; formal type of literature.
Named for the large trunk-like proboscis of its males, this giant oceangoing pinniped can weigh up to 4,000 kilograms and was once hunted nearly to extinction for lamp oil. What animal is it?
Elephant seal: Genus of aquatic carnivores.
Sold under the brand name Nexium, this proton pump inhibitor treats acid reflux by blocking an enzyme in the stomach's acid-producing cells — what is it?
Esomeprazole: Medication which reduces stomach acid.
While its deciduous neighbors drop everything and go bare for winter, this kind of plant keeps its foliage green and working all year round — what's the botanical term?
Evergreen: Plant that has leaves in all seasons.

Modern phylogenetics calls this a paraphyletic group covering nearly every vertebrate except the tetrapods — gill-bearing, limbless-of-digits, and usually cold-blooded. What aquatic animals are these?
This mathematical principle links differentiation and integration, showing the two operations to be essentially inverses of each other — what is it called?
Fundamental theorem of calculus: Relationship between derivatives and integrals.
The longest member of the weasel family at up to 1.8 meters, this noisy, highly social river-dweller lives in family groups along the Amazon and in the Pantanal — which animal?
Known as the black shag in New Zealand, this widespread seabird breeds across much of the Old World, Australasia, and the Atlantic coast of North America — which bird?
This German-American physicist won a 1967 Nobel Prize for explaining how a nuclear cycle powers heavy stars, after heading the Theoretical Division at Los Alamos during World War II — who is he?
Also nicknamed 'rose mallow,' this genus of large, showy tropical flowers includes both herbaceous plants and woody shrubs — which genus is it?
Hibiscus: Genus of plants. Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.
In its pure form it's a faintly blue, syrupy liquid, but the concentrated 'high-test' version decomposes explosively when heated and has even been used as rocket fuel — what compound is it?
Hydrogen peroxide: Chemical compound. The molecule hydrogen peroxide is asymmetrical and highly polarized.

Named for the indigo-blue line seen in its spectrum when discovered in 1863, this soft, silvery-white metal with atomic number 49 is used to make the transparent conductive coating on flat-panel displays — what is it?
Indium: Chemical element with atomic number 49 (In)
Before he proposed that the Earth behaves like one self-regulating living system, this English independent scientist built the detector that first revealed CFCs lurking in our atmosphere. Who was he?

An Alberta-born clinical psychologist and University of Toronto professor, he drew huge attention in the late 2010s for his cultural and political views — self-identifying as a classical liberal. Who is he?
Often miscalled a 'bear,' this tailless, fluffy-eared Australian marsupial is actually a close cousin of the wombat — what is it?
Koala: Arboreal herbivorous marsupial native to Australia.

Native to the dry grasslands and deserts of Afghanistan, Iran, Pakistan, India, and Nepal, this ground-dwelling reptile is so widely captive-bred it's considered the first domesticated species of its kind — what is it?
Leopard gecko: Species of reptile. The leopard gecko is a popular pet, and due to extensive captive breeding it is sometimes referred to as the first domesticated species of lizard.
Based on the L-188 Electra airliner and distinguished by a tail 'stinger' used to magnetically detect submarines, this four-engine turboprop has served the US Navy since the 1960s — which aircraft?
Lockheed P-3 Orion: Maritime patrol and anti-submarine aircraft family.
Occurring naturally as the mineral brucite, this poorly soluble white solid neutralizes stomach acid in a well-known antacid — which compound?
Magnesium hydroxide: Inorganic compound of formula Mg(OH)2.
Part of the chamomile tribe within the sunflower family, some species in this plant genus share the common name 'mayweed' — which genus?
Marketed under brand names like Quaalude and Sopor, this sedative was pulled from commercial production in the mid-1980s due to widespread misuse — which drug?
Nicknamed the 'powerhouse of the cell' after a phrase popularized in a 1957 magazine article, this double-membraned organelle generates ATP through respiration — which organelle?
Mitochondrion: Organelle in eukaryotic cells responsible for respiration.
This semiaquatic rodent swims using webbed hind feet while its scaly, flattened tail works mainly as a rudder for steering — what is it?
Muskrat: Species of rodent. The muskrat or common muskrat (Ondatra zibethicus) is a medium-sized semiaquatic rodent.
This group of three genetic conditions causes nervous-system tumors; its first type brings café au lait skin spots and scoliosis, while its second causes early hearing loss — what's it called?
Neurofibromatosis: Three genetic disorders involving benign tumors of the nervous system.

Producing a distinctive capped nut and supporting more than 950 species of caterpillar, this keystone hardwood genus ranges across the Northern Hemisphere in some 500 species, some evergreen, some deciduous — what tree is it?
Oak: Tree or shrub in the genus Quercus.
Working alongside Lise Meitner and Fritz Strassmann in 1938, this German chemist co-discovered nuclear fission and later won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry alone — who is he?
Otto Hahn: German nuclear chemist and Nobel laureate (1879–1968)
Best known for creating Gmail, this engineer also built the first prototype of Google's ad platform and once suggested the company's old motto, 'Don't be evil' — who is he?
First extracted from coal tar and now made from petroleum, this mildly acidic compound is a key precursor to Bakelite and nylon — what is it?
Widely planted along London's streets as a hybrid variety, this tree genus includes the sycamores of North America and can tower up to 50 meters — which genus?
Platanus: Genus of flowering plants constituting the family Platanaceae.

Arising over 60 million years ago from small tree-dwellers, this order favored big brains, binocular color vision and opposable thumbs to grasp among the branches — and it includes lemurs and apes — what is it?
Primate: Order of mammals. New primate species continue to be discovered: over 25 species were described in the 2000s, 36 in the 2010s, and six in the 2020s.

Known in France as the Patou and in the US by another name, this French livestock guardian breed hails from a range straddling France and Spain, protecting flocks from wolves and bears. What breed is it?
Pyrenean Mountain Dog: French breed of dog. The Pyrenean Mountain Dog (Chien de Montagne des Pyrénées) is a French breed of livestock guardian dog.

This Canadian-American inventor pulled off the first transmission of speech by radio in 1900 and the first two-way radiotelegraphy across the Atlantic in 1906, racking up hundreds of patents — seven granted after his death. Who was this AM-radio pioneer?
Reginald Fessenden: Canadian-American electrical engineer and inventor (1866–1932)
Commonly called the dog rose, this variable climbing wild plant is native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia — which species?
Also known as mucopolysaccharidosis type III, this rare genetic disorder is caused by the body's inability to break down certain sugar molecules called glycosaminoglycans — what is it called?

Sanfilippo syndrome: Rare metabolism disorder. Sanfilippo syndrome, also known as mucopolysaccharidosis type III (MPS III), is a rare lifelong genetic disease that mainly affects the brain and spinal cord.
Considered paradoxical by the ancient Greeks in Zeno's puzzle about motion, what term describes an infinite sum of terms added one after another, later made rigorous through the concept of a limit?
Series (mathematics): Infinite sum. In mathematics, a series is, roughly speaking, an addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.
The sixth most abundant element in Earth's crust, this soft alkali metal carries symbol Na and pairs with chlorine as the ocean's most common dissolved element — what is it?
Sodium: Chemical element with atomic number 11 (Na)

Developed in 1962 by an American pharmaceutical company and derived from a natural male hormone, this anabolic steroid treats hereditary angioedema and is unusual for surviving liver metabolism without being esterified — what is it?
Stanozolol: Discontinued steroid for heart treatment.
Comprising around 90 species split between river martins and all other members, this family of aerial-feeding songbirds is thought to have evolved as hole-nesters in Africa — what are they called?
Swallow: Family of songbirds. The term "swallow" is used as the common name for Hirundo rustica in the United Kingdom and Ireland.

Found at the ends of linear chromosomes, this repetitive DNA region works with specialized proteins to prevent the chromosome tip from being mistaken for a damaging double-strand break — what is it called?
Telomere: Region of repetitive nucleotide sequences on chromosomes.
The largest cat of the genus Panthera, this Asian apex predator wears orange fur with mostly vertical black stripes and ranges from snowy Russian forests to tropical Indian jungles — what is it?
Closely related to salmon, these carnivorous freshwater fish spawn in shallow gravel beds of headwater creeks after migrating upstream — what are they called?
Trout: Freshwater fish from subfamily Salmoninae.
Found in Central and South America, only three living species of this blood-feeding, leaf-nosed flying mammal exist, while two extinct relatives once roamed North America — which creature?

The smallest member of this genus, found in Great Britain, is also considered the tiniest carnivorous mammal species on Earth, with some populations turning white in winter. What group of small predators is this?
Weasel: Mammal of the mustelid family.
Known to TV audiences as 'Dr. Now,' this Iranian-born American surgeon has spent over a decade helping patients on My 600-lb Life reach life-saving weight loss — who is he?
Younan Nowzaradan: Iranian-American surgeon, television personality, and author (born 1944)
Arsenic is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for arsenic is As. Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
What is the chemical symbol for nihonium?
The symbol for nihonium is Nh. Nihonium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Nh and atomic number 113.

Paul Rudd: Paul Stephen Rudd (born April 6, 1969) is an American actor.

Idris Elba: Sir Idrissa Akuna Elba ( IH-driss; born 6 September 1972) is an English actor, DJ, rapper, and producer.

Jodie Foster: Alicia Christian "Jodie" Foster (born November 19, 1962) is an American actress and filmmaker.

Ana de Armas: After moving to Los Angeles, de Armas had English-speaking roles in the psychological thriller Knock Knock (2015) and the comedy-crime film War Dogs (2016).
In what year did Bill Paxton die?
Bill Paxton: William Paxton (May 17, 1955 – February 25, 2017) was an American actor, filmmaker and musician.
In what year did John Wayne die?
John Wayne: Marion Robert Morrison (May 26, 1907 – June 11, 1979), known professionally as John Wayne, was an American actor.

Home Alone is a 1990 American Christmas comedy film directed by Chris Columbus and written and produced by John Hughes.

Reptile (film): The film stars del Toro in the lead role, alongside Justin Timberlake, Alicia Silverstone, Eric Bogosian, Ato Essandoh, Domenick Lombardozzi, and Michael Pitt.
In what year was Nyad first released?
Nyad is a 2023 American biographical sports drama film about swimmer Diana Nyad's multiple attempts in the early 2010s to swim the Straits of Florida.

Dream Scenario is a 2023 American surreal satirical comedy drama film written, directed, and edited by Kristoffer Borgli.

In what year was Halo first released?
Halo (franchise): The series launched in November 2001 with the first-person shooter video game Halo: Combat Evolved and its tie-in novel, The Fall of Reach.
In what year was Mamma Mia! first released?
